name: Heth
title: Ancestor of the Hittites
summary: Heth was a son of Canaan and a grandson of Ham. He is regarded as the ancestor of the Hittites (the children of Heth), a people who lived in the land of Canaan and with whom the patriarchs Abraham and Isaac had contact. The Hittites played an important role in the biblical accounts concerning the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Heth's lineage from Canaan
keyEvents.description: Heth is mentioned as a son of Canaan in the genealogy in Genesis. He is listed among the descendants of Canaan who became various ethnic groups.

keyEvents.title: Heth in the genealogical line of Canaan in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Heth's lineage is confirmed in 1 Chronicles, where he is again mentioned as a son of Canaan in the genealogy.

keyEvents.title: Heth's Children and Abraham
keyEvents.description: Abraham's negotiations with 'the children of Heth' (the Hittites) regarding the purchase of the burial site in the Cave of Machpelah show that Heth's descendants were an established people in Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Isaac's Burial in the Land of the Hittites
keyEvents.description: Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham in the Cave of Machpelah, which had been purchased from the children of Heth, confirming the lasting connection between the patriarchs and the Hittites.

keyEvents.title: Esau's Hittite Wives
keyEvents.description: Esau took wives from among the daughters of Heth, which was a source of grief for Isaac and Rebekah. This shows the close contact between Abraham's descendants and the Hittites.

keyEvents.title: The Curse of Canaan
keyEvents.description: As a descendant of Ham through Canaan, Heth and his descendants were part of the curse that Noah pronounced over Canaan. The Hittites are later mentioned among the peoples whom Israel was to drive out from the promised land.
